Here's your 8-bar arrangement in 4/4 time, eighth-note motif throughout. I'll walk through it bar by bar.

---

## Bars 1–2: A Minor Statement

**Bar 1** (*mp, legato, pedal down on beat 1, change on beat 3*)

RH: C⁴ – E⁴ – G⁴ – A⁴ | G⁴ – E⁴ – D⁴ – C⁴
Fingering: 1 – 2 – 4 – 5 | 4 – 2 – 1 – 1 (shift)

LH: Am (A₂ – C₃ – E₃), whole note

**Bar 2** (*pedal change on beat 1*)

RH: C⁴ – E⁴ – G⁴ – A⁴ | G⁴ – E⁴ – B³ – A³
Fingering: 1 – 2 – 4 – 5 | 4 – 2 – 1 – 1 (tuck under)

LH: Am (A₂ – C₃ – E₃) beats 1–2, then E major (E₂ – G#₂ – B₂) beats 3–4 for the harmonic minor dominant pull

The B–A ending in the melody resolves to the tonic and closes the opening statement.

---

## Bars 3–4: Development and Sequence

**Bar 3** (*mf, pedal change each beat 1 and 3*)

RH: D⁴ – F⁴ – A⁴ – B⁴ | A⁴ – F⁴ – E⁴ – D⁴
Fingering: 1 – 2 – 4 – 5 | 4 – 2 – 1 – 1

LH: Dm (D₂ – F₂ – A₂) beats 1–2, then Am/C first inversion (C₃ – E₃ – A₃) beats 3–4

This sequences the motif up a step to D, which introduces the iv chord and adds momentum.

**Bar 4** (*slight ritardando on beats 3–4*)

RH: E⁴ – G⁴ – B⁴ – C⁵ | B⁴ – G⁴ – F⁴ – E⁴
Fingering: 1 – 2 – 4 – 5 | 4 – 2 – 1 – 1

LH: Em (E₂ – G₂ – B₂) beats 1–2, then G major (G₂ – B₂ – D₃) beats 3–4

The G major chord is the pivot. In A minor, G is the bVII. In C major, G is the dominant (V). This is your modulation point.

---

## Bars 5–6: C Major Arrival

**Bar 5** (*f, a tempo, pedal change beat 1 and 3, brighter tone*)

RH: C⁴ – E⁴ – G⁴ – A⁴ | G⁴ – E⁴ – F⁴ – G⁴
Fingering: 1 – 2 – 4 – 5 | 4 – 2 – 3 – 4

LH: C major (C₂ – E₂ – G₂), whole note

Same motif, but now it sounds major because of the C major chord underneath. The ending rises (F–G) instead of descending, which opens the phrase up.

**Bar 6** (*pedal change beat 1 and 3*)

RH: A⁴ – G⁴ – F⁴ – E⁴ | D⁴ – E⁴ – F⁴ – G⁴
Fingering: 5 – 4 – 3 – 2 | 1 – 2 – 3 – 4

LH: F major (F₂ – A₂ – C₃) beats 1–2, then G major (G₂ – B₂ – D₃) beats 3–4

This is a IV–V progression building toward the final cadence.

---

## Bars 7–8: Wedding Cadence

**Bar 7** (*ff, broaden, hold pedal through bar*)

RH: E⁴ – G⁴ – C⁵ (quarter + eighth, let ring) | D⁵ – C⁵ – B⁴ (eighths)
Fingering: 1 – 2 – 5 | 4 – 3 – 2

LH: Am/C first inversion (C₃ – E₃ – A₃) beats 1–2, then G major (G₂ – B₂ – D₃) beats 3–4

The brief return to Am color before G creates a vi–V moment, which is a classic "emotional swell" sound in wedding arrangements.

**Bar 8** (*fermata on final chord, pedal held to end*)

RH: C⁵ whole note, or C⁴ – E⁴ – G⁴ – C⁵ rolled chord
Fingering for rolled chord: 1 – 2 – 4 – 5

LH: C major (C₂ – G₂ – C₃), open voicing, whole note

Hold with fermata. Lift pedal slowly after the sound fades.

---

## At a Glance

Bars 1–2 establish A minor with the motif. Bars 3–4 develop and sequence upward, reaching G major as a pivot chord. Bars 5–6 arrive in C major with the motif reframed over bright major harmony, building through IV–V. Bars 7–8 deliver the wedding cadence with a vi–V–I in C major, ending on a rolled C major chord with fermata.

Dynamic arc: mp → mf → f → ff with a slight rit in bar 4 and a broadening in bars 7–8. Pedal changes every two beats except where marked to hold. The whole thing should take about 25–30 seconds at a moderate tempo around quarter note = 80–90.
